subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Most women are __facing the same problem__ when it comes to job satisfaction because of the pay parity in institutions.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"in the same boat"** means to be in the same difficult situation as others. (एक ही स्थिति में होना)

 
 
• **Example: **During the economic recession, many businesses found themselves **in the same boat**, struggling to survive.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, "Most women are facing the same problem when it comes to job satisfaction because of the pay parity in institutions," the idiom "**in the same boat**" can be used to convey that most women are experiencing the same issue.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Armchair experts** (अज्ञानी विशेषज्ञ): People who offer advice or opinions on something they have little knowledge or experience in.

 
 
• **Example: **There are too many **armchair experts** commenting on how the team should play without ever having played the game themselves.
 
 
 
• **A drop in the ocean** (समुद्र में एक बूंद): A very small amount compared to what is needed or expected.
 
 
• **Example: **Donating one dollar may seem like **a drop in the ocean**, but every little bit helps.
 
 
 
• **Comparing apples to oranges** (असमान चीजों की तुलना): Comparing two things that are inherently different and thus cannot be compared.
 
 
• **Example: **Comparing the performance of a car to a bicycle is like **comparing apples to oranges**.
